title: Add residency-gate middleware and KMS origin attestation
author: Liam Chen
commits: a1f3b9c: initial residency-gate middleware and spec
b7e6d2f: wire KMS origin attestation into installer templates
c2d9f04: add audit envelope signer and tests
d4a8e1e: migration helper script and helm values for residency mode
description: Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated regions require a deployment-side guard that enforces data residency policies and proves KMS key origins to downstream audit systems. This PR introduces a lightweight residency-gate middleware and a KMS-origin attestation flow integrated into the private installer. Motivation: existing region-pin checks lived only at the control plane and were bypassable during air-gap installs; we need an installer-time and runtime assertion that 1) inbound tenant configs are residency-compliant, 2) customer CMKs are bound to an allowed region, and 3) every installation emits a signed audit envelope asserting key provenance for later verification. Changes: implemented residency_gate middleware (pkg/middleware/residency_gate.go) that validates tenant metadata against installer-configured geozones and rejects non-compliant onboarding attempts; added envelope_signer (pkg/audit/envelope_signer.go) to produce RFC-compliant signed audit envelopes containing: tenancy id, key ARN/alias, key region, installer fingerprint, and timestamp; templated KMS attestation artifacts for the installer (cmd/installer/templates/kms-attest.yaml) so on-prem installers can perform a signed attestation step with local KMS or HSM; added helm values file (deploy/helm/values-residency.yaml) to enable residency-mode toggles and key scoping policies; included an integration test harness (test/integration/residency_gate_test.go) exercising permitted and blocked flows; migration helper (scripts/migrate/kek_rebind.sh) to assist operators re-binding tenant KEKs to region-scoped CMKs during residency enablement. Security considerations: signer uses customer-managed KEK when available; fallback to installer-scoped ephemeral KEK is explicitly logged as lower-trust and requires operator acknowledgement; all audit envelopes are hashed and stored in the installer audit log with transparent headers for downstream forwarders. Backwards compatibility: residency gate is opt-in via helm value residency.enabled=false by default; enabling flips admission behavior and will reject previously-allowed non-compliant tenant records until migration script is run. Testing: unit tests for middleware and signer, integration test matrix across three geozones and local KMS emulator, and an end-to-end smoke run in CI. CI: initial run showed a flaky integration test (timing-sensitive KMS emulator); fixed by adding a readiness probe and reran — CI passed. Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag; coordinate a staged rollout with installed customers via cherrypick channel; recommend operators run scripts/migrate/kek_rebind.sh in a maintenance window; record attested envelopes to customer-provided audit storage if configured. Related: references ENG-1452 for policy model and SEC-2021 for audit envelope format. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] docs (docs/security/residency-gate.md) [x] migration helper [x] security review. Reviewer notes and thread summary: Aisha: requested clearer failure modes in middleware (replies: added explicit error codes and operator guidance in docs and tests); Dmitri: asked to make envelope format compatible with existing audit-forwarder schema (replies: added normalization layer in envelope_signer and example forwarder mapping in docs); Marta: asked for a non-ephemeral fallback warning in the installer UI and a prominent helm value description (replies: added helm value notes and UI warning stub). Merge: squashed and merged after approvals. Release notes: "Installer: opt-in residency-gate middleware and KMS origin attestation; installer now supports signed audit envelopes for key provenance. See docs/security/residency-gate.md for migration steps." Breaking change: false
